_note: The Interview (DESIGN.md §2): character creation as a talk show segment. Oprah's every spoken line (intro and each prompt) is a quote from data/quotes/oprah.json, verbatim, and only quotes marked verified=true there (tests/test_quotes_vv.gd); the player's answers are the Fallout-style replies, each shifting stats. 'stats' lists the stat ids/labels; 'base' and 'min'/'max' bound each stat; 'questions' is the interview, in order: each is {"prompt": text, "answers": [{"text": text, "stats": {stat_id: delta}}]} (up to 8 answers per question). When the questions run out the stats are written to WorldState (stats, interview_done).
title: The Interview
intro: So I want all the girls watching here, now, to know that a new day is on the horizon!
Each of us in this room are celebrated because of the stories that we tell, and this year we became the story.

answers.text: I am a first-year receptionist with a dental plan. That is the full list.
Whatever the audience claps for. I can work with that.
I prefer to read the terms and conditions of my possibilities first.
Mostly I am the ability to leave a room quickly.
[Say nothing. Let the silence be a gift to the studio audience.]
Great. I have a lot of wounds. How much airtime is there?
I have kept them in a drawer, labeled and dated, in case of litigation.
I turned them into a podcast and the podcast into a second wound.
Those are not wounds, Oprah, those are my muscles.
What is the exchange rate on wisdom? I will need it in writing.

questions.prompt: There is no such thing as failure — failure is just life trying to move us in another direction.

answers.text: That is what I told the landlord, and he did not find it moving.
Then my entire résumé is just life directing me, very firmly, out of buildings.
A failure is a failure. I will take the failure and keep the direction.
I have never failed. I have only been misunderstood by institutions.
[Nod slowly. Take the quote. Sell the quote.]

questions.prompt: The key to life is to develop an internal moral, emotional GPS that can tell you which way to go.

answers.text: Mine only says 'recalculating.' It has said that for eleven years.
I outsourced it to a group chat. They are very decisive.
I follow the crowd. The crowd has never once been wrong in my presence.
I have a compass, a paper map, and a deep distrust of anything that speaks to me kindly.
It points, quite firmly, at the nearest exit.

questions.prompt: You wanna max out your humanity by using your energy to lift yourself up, your family, and the people around you.

answers.text: My family will be so thrilled to hear they are being lifted. Nobody has told them.
Who decides how high is up? Is there a rubric? Is it a committee?
Done. I have lifted myself up and away from everyone who owns a lease.
I would rather be lifted by someone I have met.
Lift them up to what, exactly? I have a fear of heights and of accountability.

questions.prompt: One of my favorite questions to ask on Super Soul is what is the lesson that took you the longest to learn?

answers.text: That 'reply all' is not a love language. It took me nine years and one meeting with HR.
That the free sample lady is not my friend. She is paid to smile. So am I, now.
I am still learning it. Is this it? Is this the lesson? Should I be writing this down?
That you can leave a party without saying goodbye. That one I learned in about four seconds.
All of them. In order of alphabet.

questions.prompt: Challenges provide opportunities that force us to search for a new center of gravity.

answers.text: My center of gravity is a bowl of cereal. It has been very reliable.
I searched for a new center of gravity and found a lawyer instead.
This is an opportunity? I would like to return it for store credit.
Gravity has always been my friend. I have been falling toward the good things for years.
Please do not ask me to search anything. I will lose my balance.
I have learned that sleep is not a mistake, and I am told that is a character flaw.
Every snack a mistake, every mistake a lesson, every lesson a snack. I am extremely well educated.
I learn from other people's mistakes, standing at the back of the crowd, nodding.
I have learned from every mistake in the comments, with strangers, for eight hours at a time.
I could not tell you which ones. I have an appointment, and I do not know what for.

questions.prompt: You have to pay attention to your life, because it is speaking to you all the time.

answers.text: Mine mostly asks whether the snacks are organic. I have a rash.
My life speaks to me constantly. Mostly it says I left the stove on.
I let somebody else listen first, and then I tell everybody I always knew what it said.
I keep a spreadsheet of everything it says. There is a column for tone.
It speaks. I lift. We each have our department.

questions.prompt: Small steps lead to big accomplishments.

answers.text: My small step is leaving this show with a free car.
Then I have taken a great many small steps and accomplished an enormous amount of nonsense.
My small step is my lunch break. It is my biggest accomplishment.
Careful, Oprah. That sentence has been a cult recruitment pitch before.
My next small step is toward the end of the segment.

questions.prompt: Everything is always working out for you.

answers.text: That is certainly something I have been told by people who were selling something.
It is! It is! Everything is working out, and it has been since birth!
I will need that in a contract, with my name spelled right.
Then why is the ship so far from land?
[Smile. Hold the smile. Hold it a little longer. It is almost a spine.]

questions.prompt: You need to make your bed every day.

answers.text: Done. I make it every morning, and then I stand next to it so people can see.
Every day is a lot of pressure. I would like to make it on Sundays, like a duchess.
My bed is a bunk on a ship with no exit. It is made. It is going fine.
Made by whose measure? Is there an inspection? Who is holding the ruler?
Yes, ma'am. Yes. Right away.
